newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-SCHNYDER BEATS INJURED SANCHEZ IN ROME.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SCHNYDER BEATS INJURED SANCHEZ IN ROME.

text.p: Unseeded Swiss teenager Patty Schnyder bundled injured former world number one Arantxa Sanchez Vicario out of the Italian Open women's tennis tournament 6-1 6-1 in the quarter-finals on Friday.

The defeat of the second seed may have stunned spectators but the Spaniard revealed later that she had been in pain with a pulled arm muscle since the opening game of the first set and had considered withdrawing.
"There was a moment when it was really bad. I felt I could not carry on but I'm a professional," she said. "I never like to give up a match."

Sanchez, who has never won the Italian Open and would have been in line to play compatriot and four-times champion Conchita Martinez in the semifinals, said the injury was one she had never previously experienced in her career.
"I couldn't lift my arm properly. It was really hurting on the serve. It happened in the first game. I hit a forehand and then after that I could not hit hard."
Sanchez added that 18-year-old Schnyder outplayed her and complimented her on her game.
The youngster was 3-0 up before Sanchez managed to stave off six break points to hold serve for the first time.
She was broken again for 5-1 when the left-hander hit a fortunate net cord that left Sanchez no chance.
The second set also saw the 42nd-ranked Swiss romp to a 3-0 lead before Sanchez managed to break back.
The effort proved in vain as Schnyder, making the first quarter-final appearance of her career, closed the match with the Spaniard taking only one further point off her.
Martinez, who has already notched up a record four consecutive Italian Open wins, stormed into the semifinals with a 6-0 6-4 defeat of South African Joannette Kruger.
In the other quarter-finals, France's Mary Pierce set up a clash with Austrian Barbara Paulus.
The 10th seed followed up her floodlit win over top seed Monica Seles on Thursday night with a 6-3 6-4 defeat of Romanian 14th seed Ruxandra Dragomir.
Any fatigue suffered following Thursday night's late game was not evident as Pierce floated elegantly around the court lashing ferocious forehands past the losing 1997 Hamburg finalist.
"I'm glad I looked that way," the 1995 Australian Open champion replied to an Italian reporter who complimented her on her poise. "It wasn't exactly how I was feeling."
Pierce gave every impression of enjoying her performance, beaming broadly at a particularly well-timed shot in marked contrast to some of the other players in action.

Martinez offered little emotion in her demolition of Kruger. The only real passion on a sun-baked centre court was the occasional frustrated scream from Kruger, who captured just 12 points from Martinez in a lightning first set.
Paulus, the 11th seed, made up for her injury-enforced absence by beating Romanian seventh seed Irina Spirlea 6-4 6-2.
Paulus was injured in 1990 and took three years off the circuit as she recovered and had treatment to her knees, ankles and wrists -- seven operations in all.
"I didn't expect too much but it is working," she said. "I think now I'm playing better than in 1990."
